author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Financial-technology company Chime agreed Tuesday to acquire nationally chartered Stride Bank for $590 million, a move intended to bring core banking infrastructure under Chime’s direct control.

Reuters reported that the transaction would give Chime access to Stride’s national charter and capabilities as it expands lending and other financial products. Chime has historically relied on partner banks to hold customer deposits and provide regulated banking services behind its app.

Investors pushed Chime shares higher after the announcement, Reuters said, reflecting optimism that the structure could improve economics and reduce dependence on outside institutions. The acquisition still requires regulatory approval, and ownership of a bank would also subject Chime to direct supervision, capital requirements and compliance obligations.

The deal is significant beyond its $590 million price tag because it reflects a broader shift among large fintech companies toward tighter control of regulated infrastructure. Closing terms and the exact timing could change during review. Any share move cited in connection with the announcement reflects reported trading at that time, not a live quote.
dek: The fintech company is seeking a national bank charter and more control over the infrastructure behind its accounts and lending expansion.
headline: Chime agrees to buy Stride Bank for $590 million
